flawed_step: The initial claim that Quicksort runs in O(n log n) comparisons on every input is unjustified. On a sorted array, choosing the first element as pivot produces subproblems of sizes 0 and n-1 at every partition.
counterexample: For the family A_n=[1,2,...,n], the comparison count satisfies C(n)=C(n-1)+(n-1), hence C(n)=n(n-1)/2, which is not O(n log n).
assessment_summary: The statement confuses swaps with the specified cost measure, key comparisons. Even if a sorted input requires no swaps, it causes maximally unbalanced partitions and quadratic comparisons.
